ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Consider point $P$ on the parabola $y=-x^2+x+2$ in the first quadrant. Perpendicular lines are drawn from point $P$ to the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, with the feet of the perpendiculars being points $A$ and $B$, respectively. What is the maximum perimeter of the quadrilateral $OAPB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Solve when $y=0$, we have $-x^{2}+x+2=0$\\
Solving this, we get $x_{1}=-1$ and $x_{2}=2$,\\
Therefore, when $0<x<2$ then $y>0$\\
Let the point $P(x, -x^{2}+x+2)$,\\
Therefore, the perimeter of the rectangle $OAPB$ is $2(x-x^{2}+x+2)=-2(x-1)^{2}+6$,\\
Since the parabola opens downwards,\\
Therefore, when $x=1$ the maximum perimeter of the rectangle $OAPB$ is $\boxed{6}$.
